subsystems.name: Regolith feedstock system
subsystems.role: mines, screens, dries and delivers the raw dust and crushed rock that is the only bulk material available.
parts: dryer or heater to drive off adsorbed water and ice
conveyor or pneumatic feed to the printer

subsystems.name: Consolidation head
subsystems.role: fuses loose regolith into solid, load-bearing material without importing cement.

subsystems.name: Mobile printer platform
subsystems.role: carries the head over the build area and places material precisely.

subsystems.name: Surface power and storage
subsystems.role: provides megawatt-scale heat and electricity, including through the two-week lunar night.
parts: fission surface power unit or large battery bank
power distribution to printers and mining equipment

subsystems.name: Swarm coordination
subsystems.role: lets hundreds of machines share one digital model of the settlement and divide the work.

subsystems.name: Structure and sealing
subsystems.role: turns printed stone-like shells into habitable, gas-tight volumes.

buildSteps.title: Survey the site
buildSteps.detail: Orbital imagery and rovers map regolith depth, ice content, slope and ground stability, and pick a landing zone beside the raw material.

buildSteps.title: Land power, comms and printers
buildSteps.detail: Robotic landers deliver a power source, a communications relay and the first small printers and diggers — no people yet.

buildSteps.title: Mine and prepare regolith
buildSteps.detail: Excavators dig loose material, screen out large rocks, and heat it to remove water and ice that would otherwise blow the print apart as steam.

buildSteps.title: Print the simplest object first
buildSteps.detail: A landing pad, blast berms and roadways are printed as a low-risk test of sintering at full scale, and they also stop later landings from sandblasting everything.

buildSteps.title: Print structural shells
buildSteps.detail: A printer lays regolith in bands and fuses each band — with concentrated sunlight, microwaves or a laser — building vaults and domes layer by layer rather than blocks by blocks.

buildSteps.title: Seal and outfit
buildSteps.detail: A gas-tight liner made on Earth is inserted into each printed shell, then airlocks, life support, power and interiors are fitted.

buildSteps.title: Scale up to a swarm
buildSteps.detail: Once one printer works reliably, many are landed; coordination software assigns each machine a region so the settlement grows in parallel rather than one building at a time.

buildSteps.title: Inspect and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Rovers and drones survey for cracks and spalling caused by repeated day–night thermal cycling, micrometeorite strikes and radiation, and repair them by re-sintering.

prerequisites.why: microwave, laser and concentrated-solar sintering of lunar and Mars simulants has been demonstrated in laboratories, but never on the Moon at building scale.
terrestrial autonomous excavators and swarm robotics exist, but nothing coordinates hundreds of machines on an unvisited surface with minutes-long communication delays.
small fission surface power units have been tested on the ground; printing whole settlements needs far more energy, including through the lunar night.
oxygen and water from regolith and ice have been demonstrated in labs, but bulk structural material production has not.
sharp abrasive regolith destroys seals and bearings, and few machines have been proven to work in reduced gravity for years.

prerequisites.tech: Closed-loop life support and radiation shielding
prerequisites.why: habitats must keep people alive under cosmic radiation for years; thick regolith overburden is the leading idea but remains unbuilt.

pathway.milestone: laboratory sintering of regolith simulants; design competitions and ground prototypes of printed habitats and landing pads
pathway.unlocks: proof that local dust can be turned into solid material at small scale.

pathway.milestone: robotic missions that print a landing pad, berm or road on the Moon
pathway.unlocks: the first real construction on another world, and protection for later landings.

pathway.milestone: one or two robot-printed shelters with imported pressure liners, visited by crews
pathway.unlocks: demonstration that printed structures can hold pressure and survive thermal cycling.

pathway.milestone: swarms printing habitation clusters and industrial structures
pathway.unlocks: settlements that grow using local material instead of Earth-launched hardware.
large permanent populations — credible only if power, autonomy, sealing and life support all advance far beyond today's state.
